text:
oliver: quick sync — we're rolling out a set of new dashboard widgets for routing policies, quotas, and per-route latency/cost. need to lock down the metric names + label (OTel/Prom) conventions before eng-runtime emits anything. who's available for a 15m?
kevin: I can jump. do we have a concrete list of required dimensions?
maria: requirements from runtime: route_id, model_variant, policy, region, pod_pool, and tenant. but tenant is high-cardinality so we prefer tenant_hash or tenant_group. also: we emit buckets for latency histograms.
tara: from SRE/console side — dashboards should support aggregated by policy and region primarily. per-tenant drilldowns will be optional (via logs/traces) because per-tenant timeseries explode cardinality.
ben: one thing to call out: alerts will target regressions at the policy level (e.g., routing=latency_fallback). so labels need to be consistent across counters/gauges/histograms.
liz: product wants a widget that shows quota consumption and enforcement counts per-customer tier + global view. we need a stable "quota_tier" label on the quota metrics.
kevin: proposal sketch (naming + labels):
```
# metric names (prom style)
redwood_inference_requests_total{service, deployment, region, model, route, policy, tenant_hash?}
redwood_inference_request_duration_seconds_bucket{service, deployment, region, model, route, policy}
redwood_quota_enforcements_total{service, deployment, region, quota_tier, route}
```
Notes: keep tenant as tenant_hash (not raw id) and do NOT attach tenant_hash to histograms that we aggregate at high cardinality.
maria: +1 but add model_variant label instead of model since we serve pinned versions. also recommend model_family for grouping estimates.
oliver: question about semantic style — do we standardize on dot.separated vs underscore names for labels? OTel uses dot-ish keys. Prom tends to use snake_case.
kevin: keep metric names snake_case (prom), but labels should be snake_case too. avoids friction in dashboards and Alertmanager.
tara: cardinality rules we agreed previously:
- free: service, deployment, region, policy, quota_tier -> low cardinality
- bounded: model_family, model_variant, route -> medium
- high: tenant_hash (only on counters when we need per-tenant billing)
Also: histograms only include low+bounded labels.
ben: what about dynamical routing labels like 'fallback_reason' — can be many values. we should map fallback_reason to enumerated buckets in the code and emit a small set of strings like 'capacity', 'latency', 'error'.
maria: implementation note: runtime SDK will expose an API to attach standard_labels map. we should freeze the canonical label list in a repo file (yaml) and version it so rollout teams can pin.
liz: action for product: i'll add examples to the dashboard PR once names are finalized. we need an example query for the Console: e.g., sum by (policy) (rate(redwood_inference_requests_total[5m]))
oliver: can we have a short doc + PR template for new metrics? owners should be eng-runtime (maria) + eng-platform (kevin).
kevin: i'll create a short RFC in the metrics repo and add the canonical labels yaml. pinging @maria to own the runtime change.
sre-bot: deploy-check: metrics-lint passed on branch metrics/label-spec; 3 warnings (possible high-cardinality labels).
maria: thanks — I'll address the warnings. plan: remove tenant_hash from histograms, and add tenant_hash only on billing counters. also will add model_family and model_variant fields.
oliver: decision summary:
- metric & label naming: snake_case for both
- canonical labels: service, deployment, region, policy, quota_tier, model_family, model_variant, route, tenant_hash (billing-only)
- histograms: exclude tenant_hash and other high-card labels
- fallback_reason: map to small enum values
- owners: eng-runtime (maria) + eng-platform (kevin)
- follow-ups: kevin -> RFC + canonical_labels.yaml, maria -> runtime SDK change, liz -> dashboard examples
kevin: scheduling 15m sync in #eng-platform calendar for tomorrow 09:30 PT. invite sent.
liz: thanks everyone :thumbsup:
